To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ScanIndel is able to recover the full indel-length spectrum with outstanding sensitivity and false-discover rate.
the gapped-aligment and split-read methods failed to recover large portions of long indels and, at the time, produced a considerable number of false calls.
the combinatorial ScanIndel approach outperforms other tools for the recovery of indels in bacterial whole-genome sequencing data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of indels in short-read sequencing data and the evaluation of four software tools to detect indels.
the detection of indels in bacterial whole-genome sequences from short-read data.
the development of a software tool for the detection and reconstruction of indels from short-read sequencing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ScanIndel was the best tool for the task at hand, and that the split-read method was not able to detect large indels.
, depending on the indel size spectrum, one or another of the tested tools might be suitable for the specific application.
ScanIndel is a highly promising tool to identify indels in bacterial genome sequences from short-read sequencing datasets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gapped-aligment approach is suitable to detect indels in short-read data, if the indel size does not exceed a certain limit.
ScanIndel is an excellent choice to identify indels, while VarScan and FreeBayes are more suitable to identify SNPs.
the combinatorial method ScanIndel is able to detect indels with high sensitivity and low false-discovery rate across all sizes of indels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the analysis of bacterial genomes, the gapped-aligment and split-read approaches are only suitable to detect short indel events.
the detection of long indels from short-read sequencing remains challenging, and that ScanIndel is a powerful tool for this task.
the performance of tools for indel detection in bacteria is highly dependent on the indel size.
